source_title: Care of adults with neurofibromatosis type 1: a clinical practice resource of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)
claim_text: In a study of 105 women with NF1 (247 pregnancies), 55-60% reported an increase in growth of new or existing cutaneous neurofibromas during pregnancy and 30% observed postpartum regression of neurofibroma size.
notes: Full text from locally supplied PDF (Genet Med 2018;20:671-682; not in PMC). Statement made by the ACMG adult NF1 practice resource citing ref 81 Dugoff 1996 PMID 8957502. Secondary citation: not independent of the cited primary work; primary paper should be read for strength grading.Patient-reported outcomes. The guideline cites ref 81 for 64 of 105 (60%) developing new cutaneous neurofibromas and 55 of 105 (52%) reporting size increase.
independence_flags: secondary citation via guideline PMID 30006586 of ref 81
